screen: /run/<id> (error): a run that stopped at Legal & covenants, reached by accepting the review sheet's Will refuse limit
title: On a failed run the refused module is labelled Interrupted while the run reads Failed, three 'Module draft rejected.' events give no reason, and nothing on the page says why the run stopped or what to change.
expected: The run page says in words what stopped the run and what to do next: CT-035 lists failed and interrupted as different run states, CT-036 says draft rejections appear as events with their reason on Run activity and Evidence > Record, PRODUCT.md says what a run could not do is stated, not hidden, and rubric D-14 says a failed module reads 'Not assessable', not 'Failed'. The same service had already said before Submit: 'No agreement is chosen among the documents, so Legal & covenants stops with "No executed governing document"'.
actual: Produced through the screen: filing only, no agreement chosen, the Will refuse limit accepted. The run page shows the badge Failed and one line 'stopped: checker' (the reason line is J1-002), Legal & covenants 'Interrupted' (the word CT-035 and the README use for a run the service lost), the nine later modules and Report 'Not run', the activity 'Run execution stopped.' and three 'Module draft rejected.' with no reason, and no mention of the agreement. The only actions are Run activity and Start from this run. The report address shows nothing (J5-007) and Evidence > Record, where CT-036 puts the rejections, exists only for a published report, so the checker's reason is drawn nowhere. The review sheet's own Documents-read line had called the uploaded file 'credit agreement · executed'.
suggested_change: Draw the module's refusal reason on its row and on each 'Module draft rejected.' event, and label the module by what happened (for example 'Refused: no agreement chosen') instead of 'Interrupted'; keep 'Interrupted' for a run the service lost. The run-level reason text is J1-002.

screen: At 390 px: / Library List view (full), /runs 'Ended without a report' (full), /report/<run>#modules/CP-6 'Published exposures and proposals' (full), #forecast 'Scenario comparison' and 'Published exposures and proposals' (full), #modules/CP-2A 'Metric' (full)
title: At 390 px six tables run past the card edge with nothing to say they scroll, and none of their scroll wrappers is keyboard-focusable or named, unlike the other 29 scrolling tables and graphs on the report pages.
expected: Rubric D-42 lets data tables scroll at narrow widths; D-35 and D-37 want every control reachable and named. The report already does this for 29 wide tables and graphs (a focusable region with an aria-label, for example 'Net debt data', 'Directed relationship map'). The Library List's Open report link and Run activity's Reason are what the reader came for.
actual: Library List: only a sliver of the Report column shows ('R', 'O'), so the way to open a report is out of sight. Run activity: the Reason column (stopped: checker) starts at x=409 in a 390 px window. CP-6: the Limit value column starts at x=495 (wholly out of sight) and 'Proposed exposure' reads 'Pr' and 'Not sup'. Forecast Scenario comparison: FY2027E is cut ('FY'). The wrappers of all six have no tabindex, role or label (CP-2A's Metric table overflows by 21 px). There is no shadow, arrow or fade to show more is there. No page scrolls sideways (scrollWidth is 390 on every page checked), so the clipping is silent.
suggested_change: Give the four wrappers the same labelled, focusable region the other tables use, add an edge shadow or a 'scroll for more' cue to every scrolling table, and at 390 px let the Library List show Open report beside the issuer name.

screen: / to /start, /start to /run/<id>, /run/<id> to /report/<id>, trace drawer 'Open in Evidence', browser Back (full), keyboard only
title: With the keyboard only, every change of page (Start a run, Start synthetic run, Open report, Open in Evidence, Back) leaves focus on the page body, so the next Tab begins again at 'Skip to content' and the reader pays 4 to 14 Tab stops to get back to the content.
expected: Rubric D-35 (logical focus order, a way to reach content) and D-38 ('if the opener has gone, focus goes to a logical place'; Fail: focus sits on body and the next Tab starts at the top). The start steps already do it: Continue to purpose, Continue to context and Review run each move focus to the new step's heading.
actual: Keyboard-only run from an empty library to a finished run and its report was completable (Tab, Enter, Space, type-ahead on selects, a file chooser). After each route change document.activeElement was the body: Enter on 'Start a run' gave /start with focus on the body and the next Tab on 'Skip to content'; Start synthetic run gave /run/<id> on the body; Open report gave /report/<id> on the body; 'Open in Evidence' and Back left focus on the body. Cost to the first control: 4 Tab stops to Start a run, 5 to Choose files, 5 to Open report on the run page, 14 to the first trace control on every report page. Escape on the trace drawer and on the Submit dialog did return focus to the opener.
suggested_change: On every route change move focus to the page's h1 or main (as the start steps do), and on Back or after 'Open in Evidence' restore focus to the control that was used.

screen: /start (Issuer ID, review sheet) and / Library home (full) with two issuers whose names share their first 40 characters
title: The Issuer ID built from the name is cut at 40 characters, so two different issuers with long names that share their first 40 characters get one ID; the Library shows one card under the later run's name and the other issuer cannot be found by name.
expected: CT-002 makes the ID the issuer's identity (at most 40 characters), the README gives 'one card or row per issuer' and AGENTS.md says to preserve source identities. One issuer must not take another's card, and the review sheet should say when the ID is already in use by a differently named issuer.
actual: Run 1 'Northbridge Synthetic Group International Holdings Limited', run 2 'Northbridge Synthetic Group International Finance plc'; both review sheets show Issuer ID 'northbridge-synthetic-group-internationa' (cut mid-word at 40). The second sheet says only 'first run of this pathway. An earlier run exists but could not be used for comparison.' The Library home then shows one card, 'Northbridge Synthetic Group International Finance plc', '2 runs'; searching 'Holdings' gives 'No issuers match these filters.'; the Holdings run is reachable only through the card's Report history, whose rows carry no issuer name. Each report's own header shows its own name. No roadmap line names long issuer names.
suggested_change: When the typed name's ID is already used by a run with a different issuer name, say so on the review sheet and make the ID unique before Submit (a short suffix from the full name), and name the issuer on each Report history row.

screen: /report/<run>#changes and #history (full), an issuer that has a run dated earlier
title: Changes says 'This is the first listed run for this issuer on this pathway' while Report history on the same issuer lists an earlier-dated run of the same pathway.
expected: CT-028: Changes compares with the latest earlier run listed when the run is made and says 'first run' when there is none; the first-run sentence is fixed by ruling 2026-11-11 Amendment 2026-11-16 (rubric D-31). The reader should not meet a sentence that the next tab contradicts.
actual: Run A (as of 2025-03-31) was made first; run B (same issuer and pathway, as of 2024-03-31) afterwards. A's Changes reads 'No earlier run to compare. This is the first listed run for this issuer on this pathway.' while A's Report history lists A (31 March 2025) and B (31 March 2024), and 'What changed' beside B opens B's own page, which says the same. The comparison rule is followed (no earlier run existed when A was made); the sentence does not say 'when this run was made'.
suggested_change: none: the sentence is ruled, so whether Changes should name an earlier-dated run listed later is the owner's.

screen: /report/<run>#history at 390 px with a 184-character issuer name (full)
title: At 390 px a 184-character issuer name fills 504 of the 844 px of the first screen on every report page, and the browser title is 207 characters; the name wraps everywhere without clipping.
expected: Rubric D-32 (long text wraps in full; nothing truncated) and D-42 (reflow without loss). No roadmap line names a long issuer name.
actual: The name wrapped in full on the Library card, List row, report header, run page and Run activity at 1440 px and 390 px, with no clipping or page-level horizontal scroll. The cost is reading order: the header is ten lines tall at 390 px, so the tabs and the first finding are below the first screen.
suggested_change: none: clamping the name at narrow widths would hide something the reader sees, which is the owner's call.

screen: /report/<id of a run that has no report> (error)
title: The report address of a run that failed shows only 'Credit report: The published report could not be loaded.' with no cause, no link to the run page and a 404 in the console.
expected: Rubric D-31: errors are an alert with a tone and an action; no raw error string. The failed run's own page has no 'Open report', so the address is reached from a saved link or Back.
actual: /report/<failed run id>#overview draws the heading 'Credit report' (not the issuer's name) and one red line; /connected/snapshot?run=<id> answers 404. The Library breadcrumb is the only way on.
suggested_change: Say 'This run ended without a report' with a link to its run page, or send the address to /run/<id>.

title: On Report history at 390 px the company band, the tab bar and the history card end 6 px past the window, so the card's right border and rounded corners are cut off; the Overview at the same width ends at 374.
expected: Rubric D-42: content reflows with nothing cut off; the other report pages keep a 16 px gutter on both sides.
actual: Right edges of the Company band, Report sections bar and the history card are at x=396 in a 390 px window on #history, and at x=374 on #overview. The page does not scroll sideways, so the 6 px is clipped.
suggested_change: Find what makes #history's container 6 px wider than the other tabs' and let it wrap.

title: The event markers on the issuer calendar and the Decision and watch timeline are 14 by 14 px buttons 2 px apart (36 on the calendar), below the 24 px target size.
expected: Rubric D-41 (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8): every pointer target at least 24 by 24 px, or spaced so a 24 px circle meets no other target.
actual: 36 buttons on the calendar page measure 14x14 with 2 px to the next target; 4 more on CP-6. Their accessible names are the full event ('Synthetic note, 2025-03-31, day, Scheduled ...').
suggested_change: Give each marker a 24 px hit area or space them 24 px apart.

screen: /report/<run>#evidence/gaps, #evidence/record, #overview, #modules/CP-3 (full) against the review sheet of the same run
title: The limits the analyst accepted at Submit (no quotes, financials that are management claims) appear nowhere in the finished report, and Evidence > Gaps says 'This run lists no gaps.'
expected: PRODUCT.md principle 2 (a limit is a decision the analyst makes) and its Positioning (what a run could not do is stated, not hidden); CT-030 (the analyst accepts each limit); CT-041 (delivery adds no analysis, a missing handoff passage stays an explicit gap).
actual: Run with the portfolio workbook and quotes left out: the review sheet listed one Gap (Security selection: 'No quotes and no price talk were entered') and two Checks, all accepted. None of those phrases appears on Overview, the Security selection page, Evidence Summary, Gaps or Record; Gaps reads 'Gaps 0 ... This run lists no gaps.' The proof's canned handoffs ignore the inputs, so a live module might state the limit; the delivery layer itself records nothing.
suggested_change: none: whether the run record should list the limits accepted at Submit is the owner's, because delivery adds no analysis (AGENTS.md).

screen: / Library home with two issuers (full), proof.serve
title: In the synthetic proof every issuer's report carries the same figures and text whatever name or date was typed, so two issuers in one session cannot show that one issuer's content stays apart from another's.
expected: AGENTS.md: synthetic regressions are labelled with their actual scope and an isolated case is not presented as a complete pathway.
actual: Two issuers ('Northbridge Synthetic Group', and one with a 184-character name) show identical leverage, coverage, revenue and cash on their cards. The canned handoffs in proof/handoffs/ are the cause (proof/launcher.py canned_handoff). Cards, search, History and Changes behaved per issuer; separation of data is unproven.
suggested_change: none: the live path or a fixture with distinct handoffs per issuer would be needed to prove it.
